title: The lotus leaf: who is the doer?
hookLine: Krishna's portrait of someone busy all day who says, inside, 'I do nothing'
carry: offer the deed; the ego is not the doer
tomorrow: the Gita's first line has people 'wanting to fight.' which word?

lines: QUIT ACTION, OR ACT? TELL ME ONE.
cards: In the Gita's fifth chapter, Arjuna is tired of riddles. You praise giving up action, he tells Krishna, and you praise action too. Which is better?
Tell me one, plainly. Krishna says both lead to freedom, but acting is the better way. Then he paints a portrait.
A person going through an ordinary day: seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, walking, sleeping, breathing. Busy from morning to night. And all the while saying, inside: I do nothing at all.

teach.b: Here's the line, Gita 5.8: naiva kinchit karomiti yukto manyeta tattvavit; pashyan shrinvan sprishan jighrann ashnan gacchan svapan shvasan.
The steady one, who knows the truth, thinks: I do nothing at all, while seeing, hearing, touching, smelling, eating, going, sleeping, breathing.
Every verb ends in -an, while doing it; gacchan grows from gam, to go. Karomiti is karomi, I do, plus iti, the closing quote. Now the teaching, one of the Gita's biggest.
Krishna isn't telling anyone to stop. The next verse says the senses are simply moving among their objects. Elsewhere he names what goes wrong: confused by ahamkara, a person thinks, I am the doer.

Ahamkara, the ego, literally the I-maker. So the answer to Arjuna is neither quitting the world nor grabbing it: do the work fully, and let go of the claim. Then verse ten gives a picture Hindus have loved ever since.

teach.h: LIKE A LOTUS LEAF BY WATER.
teach.b: One who acts, offering the deed to Brahman and letting go of clinging, is untouched by wrong, like a lotus leaf by water. The leaf sits in the pond, wet all around, and the drops roll off.

teach.h: DO THE WORK. DROP THE CLAIM.
teach.b: This is karma yoga, and it's why so many Hindus offer their work: food set before God before anyone eats, a day's work given with a quiet prayer. The busy hands stay busy. Only the I-maker steps back.

how: Many Hindus offer food to God before eating it (naivedya) and share it afterward as prasad; some chant Gita chapter five as part of a daily reading.

o: plain words that come back in text after text
a list of words found in only one scripture
rare words saved for temple rituals

games.q: the busy body and the lotus leaf — tap the pairs.
p: untouched by the water around it

s: this verse tells people to shut down their senses
it lists the senses at work; the steady one sees, hears and breathes, and says I do nothing.
the -an ending in pashyan means while doing it
pashyan, while seeing; shvasan, while breathing.
the Gita's answer to Arjuna is to quit all action
he asks exactly that; Krishna says act fully, offer the deed, and drop the claim 'I am the doer.'

games.q: an aunt cooks all day for a festival, then won't take a single compliment: 'it was all his.' which Gita idea is she living?
o: she's just being modest; she should take the credit.
karma yoga: do the work fully, offer it to God, don't claim to be the doer.
she's renouncing action, like a monk.
games.why: she cooked all day, so she didn't quit action. she let go of the claim: the lotus leaf of 5.10, wet all around and dry.

practice: Go through the list with your own body, one per breath: look at one thing, pashyan; listen to one sound, shrinvan; touch what's under your hand, sprishan; smell the air, jighran. Then rest in shvasan, breathing.
At the end, offer it the way many Hindus do, with a quiet 'this is yours' to God; if you don't pray, to whatever your work serves. Let the I-maker sit this one out.

wordCard.voice: Two hundred core words: today, the body's verbs, each ending in -an, while doing it: pashyan, seeing; shrinvan, hearing; shvasan, breathing. And ahamkara, the I-maker, the voice that says, I am the doer.

orig.note: Sanskrit: pashyan, while seeing, the first of the body's verbs in Gita 5.8.

carryVoice: For the road: offer the deed; the ego is not the doer. A lotus leaf, wet all around, and dry.

sources.q: naiva kinchit karomiti yukto manyeta tattvavit pashyan shrinvan sprishan jighrann ashnan gacchan svapan shvasan
